newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee rangebound, interest slight before NY.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee rangebound, interest slight before NY.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures again got off to a slow start in early trading on Tuesday with nearby contracts content to drift in ranges of just $20.
Traders said a lack of demand from roasters combined with Europe's August holiday period were reducing activity on the London market.
"You can't really make any judgements, it's deadly quiet. Only a little bit of activity has been seen from jobbers or people that might need to do something," said one trader.
"It's a low roasting period, I don't think it's going to pick up for a while," he added.

A similar picture was seen in London on Monday but then a spurt of buying in New York gave the robustas market a much-needed boost. Traders said London activity was likely to remain subdued until the arabicas opened.
At the midday break benchmark September was unchanged at $1,660 with the second-month November contract up $2 at $1,657.
Volume totalled 1,761 lots, dominated by the two front contracts. Traders said there had been little switch interest.
